I'm a [Pivotal Research](https://www.pivotal-research.org/) Fellow working with [SecureBio](https://securebio.org/). My research measures how much current AI models could help someone misuse biology, and how reliably model safeguards hold up. It runs in three threads:

1. **Model-agnostic eval suites** in [Inspect AI](https://inspect.ai-safety-institute.org.uk/) that separate when a model *won't* answer from when it *can't*. Most safety evals score these the same way, so a refusal and genuine ignorance look identical in the results.

2. **Threat-modeling biosecurity uplift** — sorting which technical bottlenecks a malicious actor actually faces, and which ones today's models change.

3. **Adversarial elicitation methodology** — multi-turn jailbreak sequences, classifier characterization, and mapping where a model's safety boundaries sit versus where its documentation says they sit.

This is defensive dual-use work. The evals measure risk so labs and policymakers can act on evidence.

Before this I was an mRNA scientist with wet-lab R&D experience — MSc Medical Science (Boston University, 2023), BSc Biochemistry (UMass Amherst, 2020).
